description: config:recommended's ignorePaths hides **/test/** from every manager. That silently disabled the KWOK custom manager below — added in #279 to keep the fourth Go pin in lockstep, it never matched a file, so the go-toolchain group has always shipped an incomplete bump that check-go-toolchain-sync.sh then failed. The list below is config:recommended's, minus **/test/**; a packageRule re-disables everything under test/ except that one pin.

customManagers.description: Track the Go version pinned in the KWOK e2e provider builder's generated go.mod

packageRules.description: test/ is scanned only for the KWOK Go pin (re-enabled below). The EKS PoC Terraform and the scenario manifests under it are throwaway validation fixtures, not shipped artifacts — keep them out of Renovate's way.
The fourth Go toolchain pin, in the KWOK provider builder's generated go.mod.

Every Go module update ships with the toolchain. `go mod tidy` raises go.mod's `go` directive whenever a dependency demands a newer language version (k8s v0.37 raises it to 1.26.6), and that alone desynchronizes the four pins check-go-toolchain-sync.sh compares — so a module bump that travels without the toolchain cannot pass CI.

go.mod's `go` directive is a MINIMUM, so under the default `replace` strategy every newer Go still satisfies it and Renovate offers no update at all — which is why #299 moved aqua.yaml and the Dockerfile to 1.27.1 and left go.mod on 1.26.5. `bump` is what makes the directive move with them.
Both Dockerfile base images: the golang builder stage (a Go toolchain pin) and the distroless runtime, re-resolved by digest together.
The Go toolchain as aqua pins it (aqua.yaml and the KWOK builder both report golang/go).

Tools that cannot cross a version skew with the Go/Kubernetes stack, so they travel in its PR. golangci-lint refuses to run at all against a module targeting a newer Go than the one it was built with. setup-envtest ships with controller-runtime, and kubectl and kind track the Kubernetes minor in go.mod.
The remaining CLIs aqua pins, plus aqua itself. None of them is coupled to the Go or Kubernetes version, so they batch into one PR instead of one each.
The docs site's npm dependencies. Every one of them is exercised by the same `npm run docs:build && npm run test:docs` pair, so splitting them buys nothing but CI minutes.
Workflow actions batch together; they share one validation — CI running at all.
